highlights.title: Claude Code v2.1.219: Claude Opus 5 Now Default with 1M Context
highlights.summary: Claude Code v2.1.219 introduces Claude Opus 5 as the new default Opus model, offering a 1M token context window and fast mode pricing at $10/$50 per million tokens. It also adds a `sandbox.network.strictAllowlist` setting to automatically deny non-allowlisted hosts in sandboxed commands without requiring manual prompting. A new `DirectoryAdded` hook gives developers more control over automation workflows when directories are added.

highlights.title: Claude Code v2.1.218: /code-review Now Runs as Background Subagent
highlights.summary: The `/code-review` slash command has been redesigned to run as a background subagent, meaning review work no longer clutters your main conversation thread. This is especially useful when using stacked slash commands, as the review will correctly target the intended code. Screen-reader accessibility also improved with announcements for word and line deletions.

highlights.title: Claude Code v2.1.216: Quadratic Slowdown Fix for Long Sessions
highlights.summary: A significant performance bug has been fixed where message normalization costs grew quadratically with the number of conversation turns, causing multi-second stalls and slow session resumes in long coding sessions. A new `sandbox.filesystem.disabled` setting lets you skip filesystem isolation while still keeping network egress controls active. If your Claude Code sessions felt sluggish after many turns, this update should noticeably improve responsiveness.

highlights.title: Introducing Claude Opus 5
highlights.summary: Anthropic officially announced Claude Opus 5, their most capable model to date, now integrated directly into Claude Code as the default Opus model. The announcement details the model's expanded reasoning abilities and the 1M token context window, making it well-suited for large codebases. Developers using Claude Code will automatically benefit from this upgrade when selecting the Opus tier.

highlights.title: Claude Code Has a Hardcoded Instruction Telling Opus 5 Not to Use Subagents
highlights.summary: Developers discovered that Claude Code contains a hardcoded system prompt instruction preventing Opus 5 from spinning up subagents, which has sparked debate about transparency in AI tooling. This connects to a related claim that Anthropic removed over 80% of Claude Code's system prompt for Opus 5 and Fable 5, suggesting significant architectural changes under the hood. Understanding these constraints can help you work around limitations and set realistic expectations for multi-agent workflows.

highlights.title: Mastering Claude Code in 30 Minutes
highlights.summary: This YouTube tutorial offers a compact but comprehensive walkthrough of Claude Code aimed at getting developers productive quickly. It covers core workflows and practical usage patterns that apply whether you're a beginner or looking to sharpen your skills. If you have limited time, this is one of the most efficient ways to get up to speed with Claude Code's key features.

highlights.title: 9-Minute Guide: Claude Code Installation, Concepts & Real Usage (China Direct Access)
highlights.summary: This Bilibili video provides a fast-paced beginner tutorial covering Claude Code installation, underlying principles, and practical real-world usage, with a focus on users in China connecting directly. At just 9 minutes, it's an efficient starting point for Chinese-speaking developers new to Claude Code. The video also briefly covers how Claude Code works conceptually, helping beginners build a mental model before diving in.

highlights.title: Show HN: How Well Do You Use Claude Code? — Usage Analytics Tool
highlights.summary: A developer built an observability dashboard specifically designed to analyze how engineers interact with Claude Code, going beyond simple spend and seat metrics to identify workflow inefficiencies. Unlike generic OTel dashboards that only show cost per month, this tool surfaces actionable insights about coding patterns and areas for improvement. It's worth exploring if your team wants data-driven ways to get more value from your Claude Code investment.

tips_of_the_day: After upgrading to v2.1.219+, run `/model claude-opus-5` explicitly in your session to confirm you're using the new default and take advantage of the full 1M token context window on large codebases.
Use `/code-review` freely without worrying about polluting your conversation — since v2.1.218 it runs as a background subagent, so your main thread stays clean and focused on building.

If your Claude Code sessions feel slow after many back-and-forth turns, update to at least v2.1.216 immediately — the quadratic message normalization bug fix alone can turn multi-second stalls into near-instant responses in long sessions.
